sections.h2: Where is the Cleveland County Register of Deeds and when is it open?
sections.html:
The Cleveland County Register of Deeds is in Room 151 of the county administration building, 311 E. Marion Street, Shelby, NC 28150. The office is open Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., and the phone is 704-484-4834.

The mailing address is P.O. Box 1210, Shelby, NC 28151, and questions can go to rod.info@clevelandcountync.gov, according to the office's frequently asked questions page. Almost everything on file is public record, with the exception of military discharge records. The same counter also handles passports, marriage licenses by appointment and certified vital records, so expect other visitors when you go in person.

sections.h2: Which documents does the Cleveland County office record, and how do I submit them?
sections.html:
It records the paperwork that moves or secures a house, and it takes submissions on paper, by overnight courier or electronically. The land record recordings page lists what the office files.

  • Deeds and deeds of trust
  • Easements and powers of attorney
  • Satisfactions of paid loans
  • Plats, which have been accepted by e-recording since 2019
  • Assumed business name certificates
  • Notary oaths, by appointment only

Electronic submitters use Simplifile, CSC or ePN. If you send an original by courier and include a prepaid return envelope, the recorded document comes back in it, and the office says there is no extra charge to schedule a FedEx pickup. Wills are not recorded here. They go to the Clerk of Superior Court.

sections.h2: What does recording cost in Cleveland County?
sections.html:
The office quotes $26.00 for up to 15 pages and $4.00 for each page after that. Deeds of trust run longer, and G.S. 161-10 sets $64.00 for the first 35 pages with $4.00 for each added page.

  • Copies of deeds in person: $.25 per page.
  • Certified copies: $5.00 for the first page and $2.00 for each additional page.
  • Assumed business name certificate: $26.00 to record, plus a $15.00 vendor convenience fee if filed online, for a $41.00 total through the online portal.
  • Excise tax on a sale: the office says $2.00 per thousand dollars of the purchase price.

When the question is how to put a new owner on a title, the office tells people to draw up a new deed and see an attorney. Staff will record it, but the FAQ page sends drafting questions to counsel.

sections.h2: Who pays the deed excise tax on a Cleveland County sale?
sections.html:
The seller pays, and the office collects it before the deed is recorded. G.S. 105-228.30 puts the tax on the transferor and sets it at $1.00 for every $500.00 of consideration or value, or fraction of that.

The register splits the money. One half stays with Cleveland County's general fund, and the other half, after refunds and the county's allowance, is passed to the state. Practically, the closing attorney collects the tax from the seller's proceeds and delivers it with the deed, so it shows up as a deduction on the settlement statement and is not a surprise bill at the counter.

sections.h2: How far back do Cleveland County land records go online?
sections.html:
Verified online records start in 1995, with older material available in an unverified index and as scanned index books. The available land records page lays out the ranges.

Online coverage as printed by the Cleveland County Register of Deeds.
Record setDates covered
Searchable real property index01/03/1995 to present
New unverified searchable index01/01/1945 to 12/31/1994
Searchable plat index (starts with Plat Book 19)05/16/1995 to present
Viewable images of index books1841 to 1944

Two practical notes follow from that page. Entries from 1979 to 1985 can be searched only by name and year, so you must open the document to see the exact recording date. For images before 1960 you need the book and page number, and a book such as 15-A is typed as 15A with no dash. Anything not online can be viewed in the office, and the office offers escrow accounts for faxed or emailed copies for a fee.

sections.h2: What is the recorded deed notice that arrives in Cleveland County mailboxes?
sections.html:
It is a solicitation that looks like a bill, and the register of deeds warns residents not to pay it. The office describes a mailer that asks for $86.00 for a "Property Assessment Profile" with a copy of your deed.

The same documents cost 25 cents per page from the Cleveland County Mapping Office and the Register of Deeds. The office asks anyone who gets the notice to report it to the Consumer Protection Division of the N.C. Department of Justice at 919-716-6000. The office also runs a fraud detection notification service; after signing up, check your spam folder for the confirmation email and confirm it.

If a relative is selling or has inherited a house in the county, pass the warning along.

sections.h2: Where do plats and parcel maps come from in Cleveland County?
sections.html:
The register of deeds keeps recorded plats only. Every other map comes from the Cleveland County Mapping Office at 704-484-4849, and the same office answers parcel questions asked by street address.

Sellers who plan to divide a lot should call the register before filing, because the office points e-recording filers to it for the review officer and administrator signatures that plats require.

sections.h2: What should an heir or a seller-financing seller sort out before the deed reaches Shelby?
sections.html:
Two situations need paperwork before the register can do anything. For a house left by someone who died, the small-estate route in G.S. 28A-25-1 lets an heir, creditor or public administrator file an affidavit with the clerk of superior court once 30 days have passed since the death. It applies when personal property less liens is $20,000 or under, and the affidavit must describe each tract of real property the decedent owned.

For a seller who carries the financing on a one to four family home, G.S. Chapter 47H requires the contract for deed, or a memorandum of it, to be recorded within five business days. The buyer may cancel until midnight of the third business day. Both tasks end with a recording at the Shelby counter.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about housing in Cleveland County?
sections.html:
Most Cleveland County homes are lived in by their owners. The Census Bureau's QuickFacts estimates 103,325 residents in July 2025 across 464.25 square miles of land.

For 2020 to 2024 it reports 38,850 households, an owner-occupied rate of 70.9 percent and a median owner-occupied value of $200,000. Median gross rent is $914, and building permits for 2025 totaled 555. Median household income is $58,534, and 20.2 percent of residents are 65 or older.

sections.h2: What other offices do I visit after recording a Cleveland County deed?
sections.html:
Cleveland County Tax Administration works from the same building at 311 East Marion Street, and its site lists weekday hours of 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. and a phone number of 704-484-4843. Go there for questions about the tax bill on the parcel you just sold.

North Carolina property taxes are due September 1 and are delinquent after January 5, with interest beginning January 6 under G.S. 105-360. Ask the closing attorney to confirm what has been paid before you sign. Recording is a separate step: G.S. 47-18 gives priority to whichever instrument is registered first in the county where the land lies, so a deed should reach the register the day of closing.

faqs.q: What are the hours for the Cleveland County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: The office is open 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Monday through Friday, at 311 E. Marion Street, Room 151, Shelby. Call 704-484-4834 with questions about land records.

faqs.q: Can I record a deed in Cleveland County electronically?
faqs.a: Yes. The office e-records through Simplifile, CSC and ePN, and it has taken plats electronically since 2019. Overnight courier recordings are also accepted at the Shelby address.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Cleveland County?
faqs.a: The office quotes $26.00 for up to 15 pages plus $4.00 for each added page. A sale may also carry excise tax, which the office describes as $2.00 per thousand dollars of the purchase price.

faqs.q: Does the register of deeds hold wills in Cleveland County?
faqs.a: No. The office states that wills are recorded at the Clerk of Court. Deeds, deeds of trust, easements, plats and satisfactions are recorded at the register of deeds.

faqs.q: What should I do if I get a $86.00 recorded deed notice?
faqs.a: Do not pay it. The register says it is only an offer for a property profile that you can get for 25 cents per page from county offices, and it asks that you report it to the N.C. Department of Justice Consumer Protection Division.
